key: O ye who believe! Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or (your) parents or (your) kindred, whether (the case be of) a rich man or a poor man, for Allah is nearer unto both (them ye are).
s: After rulings on women and orphans, the believers are charged to bear true witness; al-Tabari, on 4:135, reads it as schooling them against the false vouching given for the Banu Ubayriq over their theft, so that no wealth, poverty or kinship bends a witness.

evidence.words: وهذه الآية عندي تأديبٌ من الله جل ثناؤه عبادَه المؤمنين أن يفعلوا ما فعله الذين عذَروا بني أبيرق= في سرقتهم ما سرقوا … ولا يحملنكم غِنَى من شهدتم له أو فقره أو قرابته ورَحِمُه منكم، على الشهادة له بالزور، ولا على ترك الشهادة عليه بالحق وكتمانها.
evidence.gloss: This ayah, in my view, is God’s schooling of His believing servants against doing what was done by those who excused the Banu Ubayriq in the theft they committed … Let not the wealth, the poverty, or the kinship and blood-tie to you of the one you testify for carry you to false witness for him, nor to leaving off true witness against him and concealing it.
